items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: But jazz musicians are always notorious. Like Fats Waller plays...

ctx.x: No, he says that he did everything he could to make it possible for himself to sound like...
But jazz musicians are always notorious. Like Fats Waller plays... I said he played organ and he liked some organ player.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: And the record opens with the Fats saying, this is for my boy Al, you know, happy birthday, and so on.

ctx.x: these were copies of 78's commercial issue, but I didn't know about this particular thing. Fats Waller, huh? Yeah. I'd never heard you mention much about Fats before. Well, it wasn't actually a

commercial session. I mean, we just happened to be up in the station. And we, as a matter of fact, it was on my birthday then, too. And the record opens with the Fats saying, this is for my boy Al, you know, happy birthday, and so on. What year would that be? Oh, this was about 1937. And was this before Journeys into Jazz started? Oh yes, that was substantially before Journeys into Jazz. That was ten years before Journeys into Jazz.
I'm beginning to get the picture on you. So you, your activities date back before being in the jazz business, date back before Journeys into Jazz? Oh yes.
